title: Biologically informative not available deconvolution excavates hidden features in proteomics datasets.
abstract: Missing values [not available (NAs)] in proteomics arise from true absence/low abundance and technical factors. Conventional imputation often obscures disease signals by ignoring the biological information inherent in protein absence. We present biologically informative NA deconvolution (BIND), an adaptive neighborhood-based workflow that classifies NAs as biological or technical. BIND binarizes matrices to encode presence/absence and uses context-aware k-nearest neighbors with Gaussian kernels to deconvolve NA origins, enabling clustering, biomarker discovery, and an NA-weighted correlation for protein-protein interaction (PPI) inference. In a simulation derived from the CCLE949 dataset, BIND achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.93, with k = 10 and γ = 3 selected for subsequent Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE) analyses, and remained robust across biological-to-technical NA ratios ranging from 3:1 to 1:3. In hepatocellular carcinoma tissues (n = 248), BIND distinguished tumor from adjacent normal, identified candidate biomarkers, and detected cancer-specific PPIs enriched in spliceosome and DNA replication pathways. A public BIND web server offers interactive visualization and supports single-cell proteomics, enhancing accessibility. Overall, BIND transforms NA patterns from a liability into biologically informative features for clustering, endotype discovery, biomarker identification, and PPI analysis.

title: Dual VEGF and PD-(L)1 Blockade: Facts and Hopes.
abstract: VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.
journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research

title: Probing Spatiotemporal pHi and pHe Dynamics in Tumor Spheroids during Growth and Alkaline Therapy via Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy.
abstract: The acidic microenvironment in solid tumors is not merely a metabolic byproduct of the Warburg effect but actively promotes disease aggressiveness and treatment failure. Tumor alkalization therapy, which aims to neutralize or alkalinize the TME, has therefore emerged as a promising adjunct to conventional cancer treatments. In this study, we fabricated both SERS nanosensors and microsensors for parallel spatiotemporal monitoring of intracellular pH (pHi) and extracellular pH (pHe) within tumor spheroids derived from three human cancer cell lines: lung adenocarcinoma (H1975), pancreatic cancer (SW1990), and colorectal cancer (SW480). Over a 7-day culture period, distinct pHi and pHe profiles were observed among the different cell types. We then examined the pH modulation elicited by administration of sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), a clinically employed alkaline agent. Exposure to 75 mM NaHCO3 for 24 h induced a marked elevation of pHe (∼0.78 units) and a modest increment in pHi (∼0.37 units). This integrated nanosensor-microsensor system, which leverages the size effect for precise spatial localization, offers a versatile approach for elucidating the complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment and helps optimize pH-modulating cancer therapies.

title: Immunotherapy in Liver Transplant Recipients with Advanced Solid Malignancies: A Three-Patient Case Series.
abstract: The use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after liver transplantation (LT) remains controversial, because immune activation may cause allograft rejection. Evidence in non-hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) malignancies is limited. We retrospectively reviewed three LT recipients treated with pembrolizumab for advanced non-HCC malignancies at the McGill University Health Centre; treatment began between May 2020 and January 2025, and follow-up was censored on 31 January 2026. A patient with PD-L1-negative non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) achieved stable disease for approximately seven months, whereas a patient with PD-L1-high NSCLC achieved a durable partial response with progression-free survival of approximately 36 months. A third patient with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma achieved a near-complete radiologic and metabolic response after two cycles. Pembrolizumab was held after this response; subsequent liver-test abnormalities raised concern for graft injury, but biopsy showed no histologic rejection and supported treatment resumption. No clinical or biochemical evidence of rejection was observed in Cases 1 and 2. At cutoff, Case 3 was alive and receiving pembrolizumab after seven cycles. These cases support a cancer-specific, individualized risk-benefit assessment in which expected oncologic benefit, alternatives, graft history, immunosuppression, and acceptance of graft-loss risk guide multidisciplinary treatment and close graft surveillance.

title: β-Catenin Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Mechanisms of Therapeutic Resistance and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with poor patient outcomes largely attributable to late diagnosis and the frequent development of therapeutic resistance. Although advances in chemotherapy, targeted therapies, immunotherapy, and combination regimens have improved treatment options, durable clinical responses remain limited. This review synthesizes current evidence on the role of β-catenin signaling in HCC progression and therapeutic resistance, emphasizing the molecular mechanisms underlying aberrant pathway activation and its interactions with other oncogenic signaling networks. The review examines how constitutive β-catenin activation promotes tumor growth, cancer stem cell maintenance, metabolic reprogramming, immune evasion, and resistance to chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. In addition, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting β-catenin are discussed, including inhibition of β-catenin transcriptional activity, modulation of upstream Wnt signaling, direct suppression of CTNNB1 expression using nucleic acid-based approaches, and interventions targeting the immune and metabolic consequences of pathway activation. Collectively, the evidence identifies β-catenin as a central mediator of HCC progression and treatment resistance while highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target. A deeper understanding of β-catenin-driven mechanisms may facilitate the development of more effective therapeutic strategies and improve clinical outcomes for patients with HCC.

title: SPP1-CD44-Mediated Crosstalk Between Endothelial and Macrophage Subpopulations Promotes Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Progression Through S100A6 Upregulation.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) progression is driven by complex cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME), where endothelial cell (EC)-tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) crosstalk significantly influences angiogenesis and immune modulation, although the specific subsets and consequences remain unclear. Here, we integrated four single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (50 PDAC; 21 normal adjacent tissues) to profile EC and macrophage subpopulations, subsequently employing CellChat to decipher intercellular communication networks and identify altered ligand-receptor interactions in PDAC. Correlation and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses (TCGA-PAAD) assessed associations and prognostic value, while functional validation used EdU, CCK-8, and Transwell assays on PDAC cells. We identified a distinct endothelial subset (EC0) and macrophage subset (Mac2) with enhanced interaction signals in PDAC. This EC0-Mac2 crosstalk correlated with significant S100A6 upregulation, which was associated with poor patient prognosis. Exogenous S100A6 treatment markedly enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration in vitro. In conclusion, EC-Mac crosstalk may promote PDAC progression via S100A6, and this interaction pattern warrants further investigation as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential target for disrupting stromal communication.

title: A multi-responsive fluorescent probe for simultaneous detection of mitochondrial esterase and viscosity.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, with early detection severely hampered by its asymptomatic progression. Carboxylesterases (CEs) are significantly upregulated in HCC cells, making them promising biomarkers for cancer diagnosis. Herein, we report a tri-lock fluorescent probe, CMA, capable of simultaneous detection of mitochondrial CE - an enzyme closely linked to metabolism and drug resistance - and viscosity for early cancer diagnosis. The probe incorporates a CE-cleavable benzoate ester and a molecular rotor formed by an indolium-coumarin conjugated system. Upon hydrolysis of the benzoate ester, the released product displays enhanced fluorescence with red-shifted absorption through strengthened ICT. High viscosity restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses the TICT pathway, whereas the alkaline mitochondrial pH further modulates the emission via deprotonation of the phenolic hydroxyl group. These three orthogonal stimuli converge to produce a 654-fold fluorescence enhancement under coexistent conditions. Cell imaging confirms that CMA effectively differentiates HCC cells from normal cells and detects drug-induced viscosity changes, suggesting its potential for early-stage liver cancer diagnosis.
journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

title: CD36-Mediated Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Crosstalk With Immunity, Ferroptosis, and Therapeutic Resistance.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer death and is associated with metabolic dysfunction and chronic liver disease. Lipid metabolic reprogramming is a key hallmark of HCC, and CD36, a fatty acid translocase and scavenger receptor, has emerged as a central regulator of this process. This review investigated the multifaceted roles of CD36 in HCC pathogenesis. CD36 facilitates long-chain fatty acid uptake and affects oncogenic signaling and the tumor immune microenvironment. CD36-mediated lipid accumulation promotes cytotoxic T-cell function and macrophage M2 polarization and drives immune evasion. Likewise, CD36 modulates ferroptosis sensitivity by influencing polyunsaturated fatty acid-induced lipid peroxidation and redox balance. Through metabolic plasticity and oxidative stress adaptation, CD36 also contributes to resistance to chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and immunotherapy. In conclusion, CD36 serves as a critical multifunctional regulator linking lipid metabolism, ferroptosis, immunomodulation, and therapy resistance in HCC, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target for improving clinical outcomes. However, clinical translation remains challenging due to the broad tissue expression of CD36 and the lack of large-scale clinical validation. Hence, future research should focus on clinical validation of CD36, mechanistic elucidation, selective inhibitor development, combination therapy evaluation, and multi-omics-guided personalized HCC treatment.

title: NCLX Inhibition plus Ca2+ Delivery Potentiates Electroporation and Antitumor Immunity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Irreversible electroporation (IRE) is increasingly used for locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet electric-field heterogeneity leaves a low-field rim where residual cells survive, and recurrence is frequent, compounded by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, an electroporation-synchronized adjuvant strategy is developed that integrates intratumoral Ca2+ delivery with nanoparticle-mediated inhibition of mitochondrial NCLX using CGP37157 (mPEG-PCL@CGP37157). This regimen markedly enhances cytotoxicity in PDAC cell lines and patient-derived organoids and significantly improves local control and survival in syngeneic subcutaneous and orthotopic PDAC models, without overt systemic toxicity. Reduced therapeutic efficacy in T cell-deficient hosts demonstrates the importance of adaptive immunity. Mechanistically, EP-resistant PDAC cells upregulate NCLX to buffer mitochondrial Ca2+ stress. Concurrent Ca2+ delivery and pharmacological NCLX inhibition induce sustained mitochondrial Ca2+ overload, triggering immunogenic GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis. This is accompanied by enhanced dendritic cell activation and CD8+ T-cell responses, as well as suppression of a tumor-myeloid SPP1-CD44 axis, promoting pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization. Collectively, targeting NCLX potentiates the immunogenic effects of IRE and provides a translatable strategy for eliminating residual disease in PDAC.

title: In Vivo CRISPR Screen Identifies RPS19 as an Immunotherapy Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Despite the remarkable clinical success of immunotherapy, its efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains severely limited, highlighting an urgent need for novel targets and strategies to overcome immune evasion. Here, we aimed to identify key regulators of HCC immunity via unbiased functional screening and develop a targeted therapy to remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed an in vivo CRISPR-knockout screen using a 4500-gene sgRNA library in syngeneic HCC mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing of human HCC tissues and in vivo macrophage-depletion assays were utilized to dissect cellular populations and validate underlying mechanisms. We identified ribosomal protein S19 (RPS19) as a central mediator of HCC immune evasion, whose deletion in HCC cells mitigates the immunosuppressive TME. Mechanistically, scRNA-seq pinpointed tumor-associated macrophages as the key effector subset, whereby complement C5a receptor 1 (C5aR1) transduces RPS19 signals to trigger macrophage-dependent immune suppression. We further constructed SP94-peptide-modified disulfide-bond-containing nanoparticles (SNPSS) for targeted CRISPR-Cas9 delivery. SNPSS efficiently homes to HCC cells, releases payloads within the glutathione-rich TME, downregulates RPS19, reverses immune suppression, and robustly suppresses HCC progression in vivo. Collectively, the RPS19-C5aR1-macrophage axis fuels HCC immune escape, and SNPSS-based RPS19 gene-editing offers a promising strategy to remodel the TME and boost HCC immunotherapy efficacy.

title: Exploring clinically anchored therapeutic stratification and tumor-stroma heterogeneity using patient-derived 3D bioprinted primary liver cancer models.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The marked heterogeneity of primary liver cancer (PLC), together with the dynamic influence of the tumor microenvironment (TME), remains a major challenge to precision oncology. As currently available therapies provide limited benefit for many patients and robust preclinical platforms for rapid, patient-specific treatment stratification are lacking, there is an urgent need for models that faithfully preserve individual tumor architecture and cellular diversity.
METHODS: We established three-dimensional bioprinted primary liver cancer (3DP-PLC) models comprising 61 patient-derived monocultures and 34 co-culture models with patient-matched cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To explore the correlation between ex vivo models and clinical drug response, we developed a clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework for response classification. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank was used to investigate stromal regulation of therapeutic response.
RESULTS: These 3DP-PLC constructs preserved the histological features, biomarker expression patterns, mutational landscapes, and transcriptomic profiles of their corresponding parental tumors. Drug-sensitivity profiling across the biobank revealed substantial intertumoral heterogeneity in therapeutic responses. The clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework integrating ex vivo pharmaceutical profiles with external clinical benchmark data enabled interpretable response classification and demonstrated clinical relevance in patients receiving neoadjuvant or adjuvant targeted therapy. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank, combined with single-cell transcriptomic analysis, recapitulated fibrous ring-like architecture and revealed CAF-associated drug-resistant states.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support 3DP-PLC as a high-fidelity and scalable platform for personalized therapeutic stratification and mechanistic investigation of tumor-stroma interactions in PLC.

title: In vitro bioactivity profile-driven discovery of drug synergies in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combination therapy is a central strategy to overcome drug resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet systematic identification of synergistic combinations is constrained by the combinatorial search space.
METHODS: We developed a data-driven workflow to integrate two orthogonal single-agent resources for 244 drugs, including cell viability profiles across 11 liver cancer cell lines and bioactivity signatures across 1,925 biochemical and cell-based assays.
RESULTS: We calculated the correlation of the bioactivity profiles between each drug pair yielding 821 high-confidence combinations involving 190 unique drugs, from which eight anchors and a 125-drug library were selected by frequency-guided prioritization. Fixed-concentration screening of 992 anchor-library combinations in the Hep 3B2.1-7 cell line yielded 89 combinations with potency enhancement. Panobinostat showed the largest potency gains when combined with briciclib or thiocolchicine (69.5-fold and 81.1-fold lower IC₅₀, respectively). Matrix-based screening of these two representative combinations across 11 cell lines revealed pronounced concentration- and context-dependence. At optimal dose pairs, strong synergy was observed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (Zero Interaction Potency (ZIP) = 40.80 ± 4.22 with 58.53 ± 6.54% inhibition), whereas antagonism was observed in some cellular backgrounds.
CONCLUSION: This label-free integration strategy reduces the experimental burden for hypothesis-driven combination discovery and provides context-specific preclinical leads for follow-up evaluation in HCC.

title: Tumor-derived annexin A1 drives lenvatinib resistance by regulating SOX2/STAT3/S100A6 feedback loop and M2 macrophage polarization in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Lenvatinib has been approved by the FDA as a front-line treatment for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its survival benefits are limited by acquired drug resistance. In this study, we investigate the mechanisms underlying lenvatinib resistance in HCC by establishing lenvatinib-resistant (LenR) patient-derived tumor xenograft (PDTX) and analyzing their genetic profiles via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Through single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC) analysis, we find that Annexin A1 (ANXA1) is significantly enriched in LenR HCC clusters. Using knockdown and overexpression strategies, we demonstrate the critical role of ANXA1 in regulating cancer stemness-driven lenvatinib resistance. ANXA1 mediates resistance by regulating S100A6 expression, while its expression is regulated by SOX2 via promoter activation, forming a positive feedback loop with STAT3. Notably, we reveal that ANXA1 secreted from LenR HCC cells reshapes the tumor microenvironment (TME) by inducing M2 macrophage polarization via FPR2 binding and activation of ERK and NF-κB signaling, leading to decreased T cell infiltration. Targeting ANXA1 via an adeno-associated virus serotype 8 (AAV8) approach improves lenvatinib efficacy in our LenR Tp53KO/MycOE HCC mouse model, accompanied by the suppression of an immunosuppressive TME. In conclusion, HCC-derived ANXA1 regulates lenvatinib resistance both intrinsically and extrinsically. Targeting the SOX2/ANXA1/STAT3/S100A6 positive loop may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for HCC treatment.

title: Redox-responsive nanoparticles prevent post-ablation hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence by dual regulation of dendritic cells and tumor cells.
abstract: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a locoregional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the long-term efficacy for RFA is severely compromised by recurrence driven by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). In this study, we identify mature regulatory dendritic cells (mregDCs) as a key immune-regulatory population closely associated with this immune evasion. Following insufficient RFA (iRFA), sublethal thermal injury induces excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and hypoxia, which synergistically promote mregDC differentiation and upregulate PD-L1, leading to profound CD8+ T cell exhaustion. To address these challenges, we developed a redox-responsive nanoplatform for co-delivery of an ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and siPD-L1. This nanoplatform effectively mitigates hypoxia and oxidative stress within the TME while reprogramming mregDCs toward an immunostimulatory phenotype via PD-L1 silencing. In both subcutaneous and orthotopic iRFA-HCC models, treatment with NPs(siPD-L1/NAC) potently activates CD8+ T cells, suppresses tumor growth, and exhibits a favorable safety profile. Our findings uncover an mregDC-mediated immune evasion mechanism underlying post-ablation recurrence and present a promising dual-regulation strategy for remodeling the post-ablation TME to potentiate durable anti-tumor immunity.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
